Corresponding required dose9.88×
Compression43.8×

A 600-fold range of doubling time becomes a 9.88-fold range of dose, and the 3.7-fold loss of effector outside a nodule costs only $0.268^{-1/2.651}=\mathbf{1.64\times}$ in dose. The back-calculation is least sensitive to exactly the quantities we cannot measure — a structural consequence of the exponent, not luck.

It does not produce an oral CFU figure. Two conversions are missing, neither in our workbook: a plate count of the co-culture, which would turn OD into bacteria per cancer cell; and the colonisation efficiency of an oral dose. The first is a single plate and would make every number here comparable to published colonisation densities — the highest-value remaining experiment in this project. The second needs animal work. The requirement is therefore reported in the unit we have actually realised, and our code asserts reports_oral_cfu = False so that a fabricated CFU number cannot drift onto this page.

3.5 Dose and safety are one constraint

Margins on the tissue axis are ratios, so raising the dose lifts both sides and leaves them unchanged. What a ratio does not track is the distance to an absolute tolerance. Smaller lesions give less gate output (Eq. (15)) and so need more dose (Eq. (46)), and that escalation is spent out of the 21.85× colonic-mucosa margin:

Lesion radius $G(R)/G(400)$ Size multiplier Total escalation Mucosa margin left
400 µm11.00×1.76×12.44× ✅
250 µm0.206031.81×3.19×6.86× ⚠️
180 µm0.091562.46×4.33×5.05× ⚠️
150 µm0.064012.82×4.95×4.41× ❌

Treating a 400 µm nodule leaves an order of magnitude in hand. Reaching a 150 µm micro-lesion spends three quarters of the margin and drops it below the 10× requirement.

This is the result that moved most when the sensor priors were replaced§2.5. At the inherited $n_Q=2$ the same escalation left 1.36× — nothing at all. At the published exponent the gate output of a small lesion falls far less steeply with radius, so reaching one costs 2.82× rather than 8.23×, and 4.41× survives. The conclusion is unchanged in kind and much less severe in degree: a micro-lesion still cannot be reached without going under the requirement, so this is still a trade-off and not a free lunch.

The multipliers are large but finite — below the penetration depth the hypoxia arm falls to its basal level rather than to zero (Eq. (17)).

This meets §3.2's cluster result from the opposite direction: quorum sensing cannot reach a micro-lesion, and dosing up until it does is not available either. Micrometastasis is not a dose problem. Both roads lead to §3.6.

Converting the margin into a rate

A fold is not a safety statement. We convert it, using the same machinery as the efficacy side so that safety and efficacy sit on one ruler:

Criterion Rate form
Efficacykill rate ≥ tumour proliferation$\ln2/T_{\text{double}}$ (doubling)
Safetyeffector-driven epithelial loss ≤ crypt renewal$1/T_{\text{renew}}$ (replacement)

⚠️ The two rate forms differ — $\ln2/T$ for doubling, $1/T$ for replacement. Conflating them understates renewal by about 30 %.

$$f_{\text{tol}}=100\left(1-e^{-t_{\exp}/T_{\text{renew}}}\right)\% =100\left(1-e^{-24/96}\right)=\mathbf{22.12\ \%\ per\ 24\ h}$$
(47)
$$f_{\text{offtarget}}=f_{\text{target}}\,m^{-b}, \qquad m\ \ge\ \left(\frac{f_{\text{target}}}{f_{\text{tol}}}\right)^{1/b}$$
(48)

where

  • $f_{\text{tol}}$ is the tolerable effector-driven epithelial loss fraction per 24 h, set by the exposure window $t_{\exp}$ (24 h) against the colonic epithelial renewal cycle $T_{\text{renew}}$ (96 h — the midpoint of the 3–5 day range that human crypt kinetics support28; see below).
  • $f_{\text{offtarget}}$ is the effector-driven epithelial loss fraction at an off-target site.
  • $f_{\text{target}}$ is the required kill fraction of the clinical indication (0.6908 %).
  • $m$ is the margin at the site, i.e. the relative gate output.
  • $b$ is the dose–kill exponent (2.651).

$T_{\text{renew}}$ is a declared value, so it is worth checking whether anything depends on it. Human colonic crypts are about 82 cells high with a mid-crypt cycle time near 30 h28, which is the measurement behind the 3–5 day whole-epithelium renewal that reviews quote; we take the midpoint. Across that whole range the constraint never comes close to binding:

$T_{\text{renew}}$ $f_{\text{tol}}$ per 24 h Margin required (Eq. (48))
3 d (72 h)28.35 %0.246×
4 d (96 h)22.12 %0.270×
5 d (120 h)18.13 %0.292×

Every one of those is below 1.0, i.e. renewal alone would tolerate the off-target dose even with no gate selectivity at all, and a 40 % swing in $T_{\text{renew}}$ moves the requirement by 18 %. So the placeholder is not load-bearing, and this section's real content is the comparison below, not the threshold. We say so rather than presenting a derived number as though the margin had to clear it.

Substituting the clinical indication's demanding end ($f_{\text{target}}=0.6908$ %):

$$f_{\text{offtarget}}=0.6908\times21.852^{-2.651}=\frac{0.6908}{3556}=\mathbf{1.94\times10^{-4}\ \%}$$
Site Margin Implied epithelial loss / 24 h Fraction of renewal
Colonic mucosa21.85×$1.94\times10^{-4}$ %1/113,800
Colon lumen (dysbiotic)23.08×$1.68\times10^{-4}$ %1/131,600
Tumour rim48.66×$2.33\times10^{-5}$ %1/9.5×10⁵
Well-perfused tissue101.7×$3.30\times10^{-6}$ %1/6.7×10⁶

Read with no amplification at all ($b=1$, crediting the margin with nothing): $0.6908/21.85=0.0316$ % per 24 h, still one part in 700 of renewal.

Turned around, the loss criterion by itself asks for a margin of only 1.36× (fitted exponent) or 2.26× (linear, hardest target). The axis delivers 21.85×, so the margin is not marginal against this criterion — and we do not need it to be.

⚠️ But the criterion covers cell loss and nothing else. GSDMD-N is a pyroptosis executioner, and IL-1β/IL-18 release is the entire basis of our distant-control argument, so a rate of pyroptosis far below renewal is not automatically harmless in colonic mucosa. Nothing here bounds that. The loss criterion is therefore a lower bound on the margin we should want, not a statement that 21.85× is enough. We report it because a fold with no criterion attached cannot be reviewed at all — not because it settles the question.

The measurement that would bound it: IL-1β release from a colonic epithelial line at the off-target gate output, rather than at full induction.

3.6 The immune cascade

Question. Under pMMR/MSS immunosuppression, how much pyroptotic flux does distant control require? Is there a region where no flux suffices? Is distant efficacy continuous in dose or threshold-like? And which half of the supervisor's local-versus-distant question can we actually answer?

Since §3.2 showed colonisation cannot reach disseminated disease and §3.5 showed dose escalation cannot either, this cascade is the only available route to distant control. That promotes this section from optional to load-bearing. It is also the least constrained part of the project, so we keep it deliberately small and report feasibility boundaries, not predicted efficacy.

The premise the cascade rests on is not ours. Delivering active gasdermin into tumour cells with a bioorthogonal system, pyroptosis of fewer than 15 % of tumour cells was enough to clear an entire 4T1 graft, and the clearance was immune-dependent — it did not occur in immune-deficient mice or after T cell depletion29. That is the qualitative shape Eq. (49) to 6-7 encode: a sub-stoichiometric pyroptotic flux driving an immune response that does the rest, with a threshold rather than a dose-proportional effect.

What it does not give us is a number. That experiment is a different gasdermin delivery route, a different tumour model and a different species from ours, and it reports a sufficient fraction rather than a dose–response for antigen, DC maturation or priming. So we take from it only that the mechanism exists and is immune-mediated, and every rate constant below stays scenario-grade. §7's sixth item — a literature dose–response for IL-1β/IL-18 driving DC maturation — is what would move this section from feasibility toward numbers.

Model

$$\begin{aligned} \dot A &= \Phi-\delta_A A &&\text{antigen + IL-1β/IL-18 signal}\\ \dot D &= a_D\frac{A}{K_A+A}-\delta_D D &&\text{DC maturation (saturating)}\\ \dot T &= a_T\,\varepsilon\,D-\delta_T T &&\text{CTL priming, suppressed by }\varepsilon\\ \dot M &= rM\Big(1-\frac MK\Big)-\frac{kTM}{h+M} &&\text{distant lesion} \end{aligned}$$
(49)

At steady state the upstream chain collapses. With $x=\Phi/(\delta_A K_A)$ the normalised pyroptotic flux, define the immune pressure number and the cascade gain:

$$\Psi=\varepsilon\,G\,\frac{x}{1+x}, \qquad G=\frac{k}{r\,h}\cdot\frac{a_T}{\delta_T}\cdot\frac{a_D}{\delta_D}$$
(50)

Taking $K=1$ and $r=1$:

$$\dot M=M\left[(1-M)-\frac{h\,\Psi}{h+M}\right]$$
(51)

The entire cascade enters through one number. The only remaining parameter is $h$, the burden at half-maximal immune killing.

Because $x/(1+x)<1$ always:

$$\varepsilon G>1$$
(52)

This is an inequality, not an estimate. Above it, the required flux is

$$x_{\min}=\frac{1}{\varepsilon G-1}$$
(53)

which diverges as $\varepsilon G\to1^{+}$. Non-zero equilibria of Eq. (51) satisfy $M^2-(1-h)M+h(\Psi-1)=0$ with $\Delta=(1-h)^2-4h(\Psi-1)$:

$$M_{\pm}=\frac{(1-h)\pm\sqrt{\Delta}}{2}, \qquad \Psi_{\text{crit}}=1+\frac{(1-h)^2}{4h}$$
(54)

where

  • $A$ is the antigen + IL-1β/IL-18 signal, $\Phi$ the pyroptotic flux driving it and $\delta_A$ its decay rate.
  • $D$ is the DC maturation signal; $a_D$, $K_A$ and $\delta_D$ are the DC maturation rate, its half-saturation antigen level and the DC decay rate.
  • $T$ is the CTL population; $a_T$, $\varepsilon$ and $\delta_T$ are the CTL priming rate, the priming suppression factor and the CTL decay rate.
  • $M$ is the distant-lesion burden; $r$ and $K$ its intrinsic growth rate and carrying capacity.
  • $k$ and $h$ are the immune killing rate and the lesion burden at half-maximal killing.
  • $x=\Phi/(\delta_A K_A)$ is the normalised pyroptotic flux.
  • $G=\dfrac{k}{rh}\cdot\dfrac{a_T}{\delta_T}\cdot\dfrac{a_D}{\delta_D}$ is the cascade gain, and $\Psi=\varepsilon G x/(1+x)$ the immune pressure number.
  • $\Delta=(1-h)^2-4h(\Psi-1)$ is the discriminant of the burden equilibrium, and $\Psi_{\text{crit}}=1+(1-h)^2/(4h)$ the critical immune pressure above which eradication is guaranteed.
  • $M_+$ is the stable escape burden and $M_-$ the basin boundary of the origin, i.e. the maximum treatable burden.

$M_+$ is the stable escape burden; $M_-$ is the basin boundary of $M=0$, i.e. the maximum treatable burden.

Results

Two thresholds, not one:

Threshold Meaning
$\Psi>1$eradication possible — but only for a sufficiently small burden
$\Psi>\Psi_{\text{crit}}$eradication guaranteed, from any starting burden

With $h=0.2$, $\Psi_{\text{crit}}=1+0.64/0.8=\mathbf{1.800}$, and it is sharply $h$-dependent (5.51 at $h=0.05$, 1.13 at $h=0.5$). Between the thresholds the system is bistable:

$\Psi$ Escape burden $M_+$ Reduction Max treatable $M_-$
1.00.8000.2000
1.50.6450.3550.155
1.8000.4000.6000.400 (roots meet, $\Delta=0$)
2.001.0001.000

The cold-tumour penalty. The indication is pMMR/MSS colorectal cancer, which our own design notes describe as poorly immunogenic, poorly infiltrated and immunosuppressive. The one mechanism that must carry distant control is operating in its least favourable setting. Required flux $x_{\min}$ (∞ = Eq. (52) fails):

$\varepsilon$ ╲ $G$ 2 5 10 30
1.00 (permissive)1.0000.2500.1110.0345
0.50∞0.6670.2500.0714
0.20∞∞1.0000.200
0.10∞∞∞0.500
0.05∞∞∞2.000

For $\varepsilon$ in the range 0.05–0.2, the cascade gain must exceed roughly 5–20 before distant control is possible at all. Converting a cold tumour to a hot one is the stated rationale for using pyroptosis; this is an estimate of how much conversion is needed. And because our simplifications all err the same way — linear CTL priming with no clonal expansion, a constant $\varepsilon$, no immune memory — 5–20 is a lower bound.

A small $\varepsilon$ is the whole reason this section exists rather than being replaced by a checkpoint inhibitor. In the trial that established mismatch-repair status as the predictor, pembrolizumab gave an objective response in 0 of 18 mismatch-repair-proficient colorectal cancers, against 40 % in the deficient arm30. Our indication is the 0-of-18 arm. We do not fit $\varepsilon$ to that number — a response rate is not a priming suppression factor — but it is why we sweep $\varepsilon$ at the suppressed end instead of a neutral one, and why the conclusion below is a feasibility boundary rather than a predicted benefit.

Clinical implication of bistability: there is a maximum treatable distant burden, so distant efficacy is not a continuous function of dose. Whether the burden is inside the basin when treatment starts matters more than how much is given. Treating early beats treating more — a stronger statement than §3.3's "clearance matters more than frequency".

Answering the local-versus-distant question honestly — one half is answerable and one is not:

Status
Local✅ measurable: 15.8 % killing at 10 OD for the construct we build
Distant❌ not measurable; this model gives feasibility only, never a number. Any specific percentage would be invented.

So the honest answer is three sentences: distant killing is the only mechanism that can address disseminated disease; in MSS/pMMR it requires a cascade gain above 5–20, which is not a low bar and is a lower bound; and it is threshold-like, with a maximum treatable burden, so early treatment beats more treatment.

⚠️ This whole section is scenario-grade. Neither $G$ nor $\varepsilon$ nor $h$ nor $x$ is measured, and nothing in our dataset could check them. The cheapest step toward numbers is literature work, not wet work: anchoring $x$ to an IL-1β/IL-18 → DC maturation dose response. Until that exists, this section reports no absolute efficacy figure.

4. Validation

Question. The evidence grade validation has been empty, on the grounds that there is no second dataset. Does that reason hold? Which conclusions can actually be put at risk — and does the protocol have the power to reject anything?

A held-out prediction does not need a second dataset. It needs a fit denied part of the first one, then asked to produce the part it was denied. Four such tests exist in our data, each one bearing on a conclusion the project actually uses, and all four pass. Tolerances were fixed as module constants before any test was run, and a fifth entry is included precisely because it fails, to show the protocol can reject. This is internal validation and we call it that: there is one dataset and there will not be another this cycle.

$$\left|\frac{\hat y}{y}-1\right|\le\text{tol}_{\text{ratio}}=0.25, \qquad \frac{|\hat y-y|}{\mathrm{SE}}\le\text{tol}_{\text{SE}}=2$$
(55)
Test $n$ Passed Worst ratio What a failure would have falsified
Dose–kill curve, leave one dose out661.165the back-calculated dose§3.4
Gate corners at 24 h, leave one out441.022the AND-logic claim§1.1
Gate corners at 9 h (expected to fail)404.447nothing — this is the power check
24 h capacity forecast from $t\le12$ h881.080every density on the tissue axis§2.1,§2.4
Dose–kill exponent refitted per construct66—the cube law, hence §3.4's robustness argument
Total2824 pass, 4 reject by design

4.1 The strongest test: the gate predicts its own corners

A multiplicative gate means the four corners are additive in probit units, so any three determine the fourth:

$$\hat z_{H}=z_i+z_j-z_k, \qquad \hat p_{H}=\Phi(\hat z_{H})$$
(56)

where

  • $z$ is the probit-transformed positive fraction and $p$ the positive fraction of cells above the gate.
  • $\Phi(\cdot)$ is the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution.
  • $\hat z_{H}$ and $\hat p_{H}$ are the probit value and positive fraction predicted for the held-out corner $H$.
  • $z_i$, $z_j$ and $z_k$ are the probit values of the three observed corners.

Holding out the fully-on corner and predicting it from the other three:

$$\hat z_D=0.9525+(-0.4761)-(-1.6044)=2.0808 \ \Longrightarrow\ \hat p_D=\Phi(2.0808)=\mathbf{98.13\ \%}$$

against an observed 98.08 % — an error of 0.05 percentage points.

All four corners pass, worst ratio 1.022. The AND claim is therefore an out-of-sample prediction, not only an internal consistency test: the held-out corner was not used to produce the number that predicts it.

The test is run at the mid-course timepoints too, and there it is designed to fail. §1.1 established that the gate is super-multiplicative while it is still turning on, and concluded that the AND claim belongs to the endpoint. That is a statement about where this model applies, made before the holdout was run. The mid-course rows check it:

Timepoint Corners passing Worst ratio Status
6 h0 / 41.60outside the claimed domain
9 h0 / 44.45outside the claimed domain
24 h4 / 41.022the claim

The boundary falls exactly where §1.1 put it, which is what makes the 24 h agreement worth something — §4.2 takes that argument up.

Everything downstream consumes the 24 h factorisation — §2.1's tissue axis, §2.2's size turn-on, §3.4's dose. and_logic_holds_at_the_endpoint_only() asserts all three legs (the endpoint predicts, the mid-course does not, the holdout has power), so the scope of the claim cannot quietly decay.

4.2 The protocol has power, because it rejects

The 9 h holdout fails on all four corners at 3.24 standard errors, and it is meant to. The 6 h holdout fails too.

A protocol that passed everywhere would have no power, and its passes would carry no information. The 9 h timepoint carries a genuine interaction term (§1.1: $+1.135\pm0.350$, $p\approx0.01$), so the holdout is obliged to reject it. We assert "endpoint passes and mid-course fails" as a single test.

A methodological by-product: the 6 h corners pass the SE criterion (±1.18 < 2) but fail the ratio criterion (0.488×). The two criteria in Eq. (55) are not redundant — the SE criterion is lenient where replicate scatter is large, and the ratio criterion is not. Both are needed.

4.3 The capacity forecast, and a bias that cancels

Forecasting the 24 h plateau from $t\le12$ h overshoots by 5.0 % across all eight curves, consistent with the creep phase that no three-parameter sigmoid reproduces§1.3. All eight still pass.

The interesting part is what happens to the quantity the degron decision actually uses. Eq. (23) rests on a ratio, not on either plateau:

$$\hat r_{\text{biomass}} =\frac{\beta_{\text{untagged}}K_{\text{untagged}}}{\beta_{\text{tagged}}K_{\text{tagged}}} \ \longrightarrow\ r_{\text{biomass}} \quad\text{when}\ \beta_{\text{untagged}}\approx\beta_{\text{tagged}}$$
(57)
Condition Forecast ratio Observed Error
Aerobic + lactate (the one the criterion uses)0.587120.584750.41 %
Anaerobic + lactate0.888090.915933.04 %

Both strains are read high by nearly the same factor, so the ratio is reproduced far better than either of its components — and the ratio is what the decision depends on. This is out-of-sample evidence for the design choice of working in ratios rather than absolute values.

4.4 The exponent, refit per construct

Construct $b$ $r^2$ Carries effector? In headline fit?
gfp5.1050.9591❌❌
GSDMD3.9560.9806✅❌
gfp-TAT3.0660.9448❌❌
GSDMD-SsrA3.0590.9856✅✅
GSDMD-TAT2.3290.9994✅❌

Five of these six are data the headline fit never used. All six exceed 2, and the headline interval 2.651–3.376 sits inside the spread. Point values are not transferable (they span 2.3×), but the sign of the curvature is:

Even the constructs carrying no effector at all are supra-linear, so "dose cubed" is a property of how dose enters this system, not of the effector. That is why §3.4's answer is insensitive to which control is subtracted.

4.5 What this validation does and does not cover

  • Not external validation. One workbook; all holdouts are internal.
  • It cannot detect an error shared by the whole dataset — a calibration offset, or a block-level scaling factor. We know that class of error is real here, because we found one§5.1, and we found it by checking internal consistency. Cross validation would never have shown it.
  • It touches no scenario parameter. $n_Q$, $\lambda_{\text{AHL}}$, the repression strengths, $G$, $\varepsilon$ — none of these are in the data, so none can be held out.
  • What it does rule out is a fit that only reproduces the points it was handed, which is the failure mode three-point curves and four-corner designs are most prone to.

The validation column in our evidence table therefore reads "internal cross validation, one workbook" — not "independent dataset".

5. Limitations: what this model cannot tell you

We have written the assumptions and gaps out module by module in the repository. This section is the summary. Where a limitation changes a specific conclusion we have also said so next to that conclusion. Every limitation here that an experiment could settle is costed and ranked in §7.

5.1 The data we have is all the data there is

Our workbook was frozen on 8 October. We asked the wet lab whether anything else was coming and the answer was no: no animal work this cycle, no lactate gradient, no inactive-GSDMD control, no empty-vector control, and nothing at 0 % oxygen. The gaps below are permanent for this year, not a to-do list.

Three specific holes in the blocks we do have.

The reporter intensity block records undetected measurements as 0, and there are 19 of them. Sixteen are contradicted by the percent-positive block measured on the same samples, which reports 2–32 % positive cells where the intensity read zero. Those zeros are the instrument's floor, not darkness. We keep them in the means and we refuse to let them be denominators. One group — 1 % oxygen with lactate at 24 h — reads 40433, 32134 and 0; we print all three, because a mean with an SD would imply a noise model that is not there.

Two measurements are missing. GSDMD at 8 OD has $n=2$, and GSDMD-TAT against L929 has $n=2$ with both values exactly 10.0, so its SD is zero and no $t$ test exists for that pair. Separately, GSDMD at 10 OD reads 14.3, 26.0 and 26.7, where the low measurement is 55 % of the other two. That group is the control for our SsrA argument, so we have used it as a range.

We also found a block-level error, and it is worth stating plainly. Blocks 5 and 6 sit about 7.6-fold apart for every construct measured independently in both, and two of the block-6 cancer rows are block-5 numbers copied across, replicate for replicate. Every cross-block ratio built on those rows is withdrawn — including a selectivity index of 11.4× and a potency cost of 4.70× that would have inverted the SsrA decision§2.4. One convention now forbids cross-block pairing, and it retired both numbers at once.

5.2 Nothing in our data identifies a sensor parameter

The reporter experiment has two oxygen levels and two lactate levels. Two points do not locate a midpoint or a slope. Every $EC_{50}$, Hill coefficient and basal level in this model is therefore a literature prior or a declared value, including the three the gut-lumen ceiling depends on. They are all marked scenario in §6.

The one we would most like to have is the quorum Hill coefficient. It multiplies everything in the hypoxia and density path, its total-order Sobol index at the bottleneck is 3.4× its first-order index, and both of the wide ranges we inherited from last cycle turn out to be that one coefficient rather than a measurement spread§2.1,§2.2. An exogenous AHL dose response on pLux would fix it in an afternoon. We did not get to it.

Two of these priors are not as unconstrained as that paragraph implies, and we would rather say so than let the reader assume the worst. $n_Q$ and $K_{O_2}$ — the two the Sobol analysis puts first — both have published measurements on comparable parts, and §2.5 evaluates the model at them. The honest statement is narrower than "nothing identifies a sensor parameter": nothing in _our_ data identifies one, and for two of them a published measurement on a comparable part is better than the value we inherited — so we adopted it. $n_Q$ and $K_{O_2}$ are graded literature_prior in §6, and every number on this page is computed at them. §2.5 records what the inherited priors gave, so the change is auditable rather than silent.

One more of this kind. The fold changes from the probit inversion — 17× for oxygen and 642× for lactate — are proportional to the cell-to-cell spread of expression, and a group mean plus a positive fraction cannot resolve that spread. We report them as conditional on it and build nothing on them. The multiplicativity test itself does not use it, which is why that is the claim we lead with.

5.3 The assumption that would change the answer

This has its own section above§2.3.4. The short version: the luminal safety argument turns on the colon lumen being anoxic while the tumour core is not, and we have data at 1 % oxygen and none at 0 %. If the native repression does not engage at 0 %, the luminal sites go from 23–60× to 0.23–0.60× and the bottleneck moves, along with the recommendation against a de-repressed promoter.

Every other open parameter here widens an interval when it is wrong. This one flips a sign. One plate settles it.

5.4 Where the modelling is thin

The dose–kill curve is three points. It fits well ($r^2>0.995$), but three points say nothing about a plateau or a threshold, so the inversion refuses to report anything more than threefold outside the measured range, in either direction — and §3.4 flags the one row that breaches it.

Killing in culture over 24 h is not an in vivo kill rate. Every cell in the culture meets the bacteria; in a tumour only the colonised part does. We handle this with a declared delivery efficiency and show the cube law makes the answer insensitive to it — but "insensitive to a number we made up" is still a number we made up.

The off-target margin is converted using epithelial renewal, which covers cell loss and nothing else. GSDMD-N is a pyroptosis executioner and the IL-1β/IL-18 release it causes is the entire basis of our distant-control argument, so a rate of pyroptosis well under the renewal rate is not obviously harmless in colonic mucosa. We have no bound on that at all.

The immune cascade is scenario-grade from start to finish. None of its parameters are measured and nothing in our dataset could check them. It gives feasibility boundaries and we have tried hard not to let it read as a prediction.

Our dosing model contains no mechanism by which a colony can go extinct, so the conclusion that redosing adds nothing is a property of how we built the model§3.3. It is flagged in code so it cannot be quoted as a result.

Two boundary conditions, no decision between them. Intra-nodule flatness differs 1.5–2× between the free-field and washout treatments§3.1. We report both, which means "how flat is the field inside a nodule" is a question this project answers only as an interval.

Oxygen is in gas-phase percent throughout, because that is how the reporter was calibrated, at 21 % and 1 %. Tissue pO₂ is lower. The directional statements survive the conversion; any absolute number would need it done properly.

5.5 Things we are still unhappy about

The selectivity index is 3.3×, from one experiment at $n=3$. It is the only protein-level selectivity figure that survived our audit and it is not a large number. The safety case rests on the circuit's tissue selectivity — which is what an AND gate is for — but we would be happier if the effector pulled more weight.

We cannot explain why the chassis-only controls curve up with dose nearly as steeply as the effector constructs. EcN alone kills 1.1, 1.2 and 3.6 % across the three doses, and the GFP strain 0.3, 0.8 and 4.2 %. Something about dense bacteria is killing CT26 in this assay and it is not the effector. Subtracting it keeps the net analysis sound, and §4.4's per-construct refit turns the puzzle into a result — supra-linearity is a property of the assay, not the effector — but we still do not know the mechanism.

Last, the tidiness bothers us a little. The cluster result and the dose result reach the same boundary from opposite directions. The growth forecast's bias cancels in exactly the ratio the degron decision depends on. The Sobol residuals land where the log-scale argument predicts. We have checked all of these and they hold. But a model in which everything agrees is a model that ought to be checked by someone who did not build it, and that has not happened yet.

6. Parameters

Every number the model uses, with its unit, its bounds where it has them, how it was arrived at and what it is for.

The table is generated from config/parameters.csv, and src/parameters.py resolves each row against the constant the code actually uses and fails the test suite if the two disagree, so neither this page nor the published one can hold a stale copy.

Five grades rather than the usual three. Calibration is fitted to our data, literature prior is measured by someone else on a comparable system, scenario is a value we declared, derived is computed from other entries, and protocol is a threshold we fixed before using it.

The literature-prior grade was added on 2026-10-14, when two parameters the sensitivity analysis puts first — $n_Q$ and $K_{O_2}$ — turned out to have published measurements behind them and were promoted out of scenario§2.5. Keeping the two apart matters: "somebody measured this on a similar part" and "we picked this" are different claims, and the old four-grade scheme printed them identically.

The census is worth stating plainly: 20 of 36 entries are scenario-grade, 2 carry a published measurement, and only 5 are fitted to our own data. That is the honest shape of a one-cycle model, and it is why the load-bearing arguments here are built to hold for any value of the parameters they involve:

7. Future improvements: the experiments we would run next

Ranked by information per unit cost, from our own sensitivity analysis rather than from intuition.

# Experiment Cost What it settles
1Reporter at 0 % vs 1 % O₂, lldPRD-onlyone plate§2.3.4's sign-change assumption — 46 % of bottleneck variance§2.5
2Plate count of the co-culture (6/8/10 OD)one plateconverts every dose in §3.4 from "relative to 10 OD" into MOI, comparable to published colonisation densities
3Exogenous AHL dose response on pLuxone afternoon$n_Q$ — the single parameter behind both inherited wide ranges§2.1,§2.2
4Per-sample spread of log-fluorescence (CV or robust SD, gated and ungated)one cytometry runidentifies $\sigma$, turning §1.1's σ-conditional folds into measurements
5IL-1β release from a colonic epithelial line at off-target gate outputone plate + ELISAthe only bound on §3.5's inflammation gap
6Literature: IL-1β/IL-18 → DC maturation dose responsedesk workanchors $x$ in §3.6, moving the cascade from feasibility toward numbers

Four of the six are a single plate or an afternoon, and each one is here because the sensitivity analysis named it, not because it seemed interesting. That ranking is itself a model output: §2.5 shows 81 % of the bottleneck variance sitting on two parameters, and items 1 and 3 are those two parameters.
